affectedPublicSurfaces: demo.app-juli.com `/decisions` -- the Decisions tab (`apps/demo/src/app/decisions/page.tsx` -> `components/decisions-page-client.tsx` -> `components/recommendations-view.tsx` -> `components/recommendations-panel.tsx`). Today one flat ranked list; after this slice, one list per `recommendation.workflow_name`, each ordered by deadline ascending where the workflow has one, else by basis recency descending, with each row rendering its own subject (product, dispatch window, or SKU set).

demo.app-juli.com `/decisions/recommendations/[recommendationId]` -- the plan-review detail a row navigates into (`components/recommendation-review.tsx` -> `plan-review-card.tsx`). Not restyled here, but its entry href is produced by the regrouped list, so a broken href is this slice's regression.

`packages/contracts/src/decisions.ts` -- the `DemoDecisionItem` / `DemoDecisionRecommendation` envelope this surface types against. #1703 puts the subject and deadline fields on it; this slice is their first consumer and adds no field of its own. `workflow_key` stays ABSENT (ADR-084 d.3).
`packages/contracts/src/seller-copy.ts` -- `SELLER_COPY_BANNED_PATTERNS`, the shared guard every rendered string on the regrouped lists is checked against.

CONTRADICTION WITH THE ISSUE BODY, verified in this tree on 2026-09-08 -- the executor must not go looking for wiring that does not exist. The issue says the panel "renders one flat ranked list from `lib/recommendations.ts::fetchRecommendations()`". It does NOT: `recommendations-panel.tsx` imports `recommendationFixtures` (a hardcoded fixture array) and `buildRecommendationDetailHref`, and grep shows `fetchRecommendations` has exactly ONE caller in the whole app -- `src/__tests__/recommendations-routing.test.ts`. Worse, `fetchRecommendations` targets `DEMO_RECOMMENDATIONS_API_PATH = "/v1/demo/recommendations"`, a route that does not exist in the backend (`ux-surface.md` A), NOT `/v1/demo/decisions`. The repointing this issue assumes has already happened is #1320's, and #1320 is not landed in this tree. So this slice's honest starting point is a fixture-fed panel, and the dependency on #1703 + #1320 is REAL: if the panel still has no envelope to group, report the unmet dependency instead of grouping the fixtures and calling it done.

SECOND CONTRADICTION, and a live taxonomy leak: the plan-review detail route's dynamic segment IS the workflow key today -- `decisions/recommendations/[recommendationId]/page.tsx` passes `recommendationId` straight into `<RecommendationReview workflowKey={recommendationId} />`. The regrouped list must build its hrefs from the envelope's own item `id`, not from a workflow key; do NOT widen that leak, and if the detail route cannot be reached without one, STOP AND REPORT (it is #1793's and #1703's boundary, not this slice's to redesign).

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Pre-merge: vitest (jsdom) component tests run from the worktree root through the workspace filter, so the suite resolves THIS worktree's `apps/demo` and `packages/contracts` and not a stale sibling checkout. Post-deploy: the candidate demo is reached only through the restricted test listener/hostname -- zero public traffic, `candidatePublicTrafficPercent` 0, stable serving 100% -- and the walk is done in a real browser so a missing JS chunk shows up as a broken surface rather than as a green status code.
candidateVerificationJourney.notes: apiSideEffectsInScope is FALSE: this slice only READS `GET /v1/demo/decisions` on the signed-in path and writes nothing. workersDisabledOnCandidate is TRUE per ADR-035 -- no background worker is needed to render a list. syntheticShopRequired is TRUE: the signed-in candidate walk reads decisions for the dedicated Synthetic shop, never a live merchant's.

journeys.name: per-workflow-decision-lists-ordered-and-subject-shaped
assertions: pre-merge: a captured decisions envelope carrying items under THREE different `workflow_name` values renders THREE lists, each headed by its workflow's seller-facing name, no item in two lists, and NO merged all-decisions list anywhere in the rendered tree -- asserted by scanning the tree, so a hidden or collapsed merged list still fails (src/__tests__/decisions-per-workflow-lists.test.tsx::renders_one_list_per_workflow_and_no_merged_list)

pre-merge: ordering is a RELATIONSHIP, not a fixed sequence -- permute the payload's array order and assert the rendered order is unchanged: deadline ascending in a list whose items carry deadlines, basis recency descending in one that carries none, and ONE comparator applied per list rather than a per-workflow special case (src/__tests__/decisions-per-workflow-lists.test.tsx::orders_by_deadline_then_by_basis_recency)

pre-merge: a product subject, a dispatch-window subject and an SKU-set subject each render in their OWN shape from the envelope's subject fields, and a non-product subject never renders a product label or a product placeholder (src/__tests__/decisions-per-workflow-lists.test.tsx::renders_each_subject_type_in_its_own_shape)

pre-merge: every rendered value traces to a field -- mutate its source field in the captured envelope and the rendering changes; no count, deadline or subject label is computed client-side; and no rendered string contains a workflow key, tool name or `subject_ref` (src/__tests__/decisions-per-workflow-lists.test.tsx::every_rendered_value_traces_to_the_envelope_and_leaks_no_identifier)

pre-merge: EVERY seller-facing string this surface renders is collected from the RENDERED tree (not from a hand-listed constant array) and checked against `SELLER_COPY_BANNED_PATTERNS` imported from `packages/contracts/src/seller-copy.ts` -- the shared `packages/contracts/seller-copy-banned-patterns.json` source, never a local copy of the list (src/__tests__/decisions-per-workflow-lists.test.tsx::seller_strings_pass_the_banned_pattern_guard)

pre-merge: every test input is a CAPTURED contract payload -- the golden fixtures in `packages/contracts/src/` and the tool-captured golden scenarios (#1311) -- driven through the real TypeScript contract types. Hand-authored event or envelope JSON is NOT an acceptable input (ADR-084 d.2); a shape the capture tool cannot yet produce is a gap in the tool, not a licence to type one out

post-deploy: each route below returns HTTP 200 as a RENDERED document on the candidate listener with the replayed scenario loaded -- not a 200 shell whose JS chunk 404s: `/` (the shell that links into Decisions); `/decisions` (the per-workflow lists); `/decisions?tab=in-progress` (the same document, query-param view -- proves the regroup did not break the sibling view); `/decisions/recommendations/<a concrete id from the replayed scenario>` (the detail a row navigates into; the segment is dynamic, so probe a real id, never the literal bracket form) -- probed with `discoverFromHtml` so every <script>/<link> the document names is fetched and asserted 200 (ADR-035's build-integrity clause: a green /health and a 200 HTML document have both been true while the app was unusable)

post-deploy: signed in on the candidate against the Synthetic shop, the Decisions tab shows one list per workflow ordered as specified, and each row's subject reads as what it is about -- a dispatch window reads as a dispatch window, not as a product

post-deploy: the anonymous door ("Dung thu Demo") is opened on the candidate and the browser network log shows ZERO requests to any `/v1/*` path for the whole walk (ADR-094 d.1) -- the replay is client-side content with no session, no auth.users row and no Postgres write; a single `/v1/*` call from that door fails the release, because it would be the #1283 shape returning
post-deploy: the candidate `/health` and one authenticated decisions read return what they returned before the deploy -- this slice adds no field to any response model

htmlRoutes: /decisions/recommendations/<concrete recommendation id from the replayed scenario>
staticAssetChecks.notes: The per-workflow list components must be present in the BUILT output, not only in `apps/demo/src`. The named failure mode in the issue's own release-evidence section is a route that 500s on a missing chunk, which a localhost health check and an HTTP status probe both miss. Route shapes verified against `apps/demo/src/app/` in this tree on 2026-09-08: the only page.tsx files under /decisions are `decisions/page.tsx`, `decisions/recommendations/[recommendationId]/page.tsx` and `decisions/in-progress/[executionId]/page.tsx`. There is NO `/decisions/in-progress` and NO `/decisions/recommendations` index route -- the In-Progress view is the SAME HTML document at /decisions under the `?tab=in-progress` query param (`recommendations-view.tsx` reads `searchParams.get("tab")`). Earlier plans (#1314, #1318) named those two as routes; probing them as HTML routes would 404 and the probe must not be written that way.

migrationCompatibility.notes: NO SCHEMA CHANGE. The subject and deadline fields this list reads are #1703's, on an existing response model; the decisions route is unchanged. This slice's whole diff is under `apps/demo/**` and `packages/contracts/src/**`; it opens no migration file, and the migration numbers for the backend slices it depends on are RESERVED BY META and never read from head. If a test cannot pass without a column or an endpoint, the dependency is unmet and the answer is to stop and report, not to write a migration or a second route. Stable and candidate are compatible because the previous bundle simply does not render the new surface, and the rows and routes it reads are unchanged by this slice.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge, discard the candidate bundle, keep the retained previous bundle serving 100%. Nothing is partially applied: the flat list keeps rendering exactly as it does today, because the grouping is entirely client-side.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Redeploy the retained previous demo bundle. The grouping is additive on the client, so reverting restores the flat ranked list -- and that MUST be a visible regression (one list where there were three), never a silent one: assert the rollback by looking at the rendered Decisions tab, not at a 200 status code.
rollbackAssertion.notes: The PREVIOUS demo bundle is RETAINED and stays serving 100% of public traffic until the candidate passes; rollback is redeploying that retained bundle. Rollback is NOT automatic for this slice: the failure modes here are visual and structural (a surface that renders blank, a chunk that 404s), which a health probe does not catch, so a human reads the candidate journey and decides. No schema step is involved in either direction.

doNotInfer: Do NOT add a surface. v1's seller surfaces are the seven S-FR-1 names -- card, plan review, confirmation sheet, run view, completion message + exception list, notification centre, deadline list -- plus the single deadline view added by the owner waiver of 2026-09-05 (#1790, and ONLY #1790). A slice that believes it needs an eighth surface, a new tab, a new modal shell or a new route is a signal the routing or the design is wrong: STOP AND REPORT, do not build it.

Do NOT hand-author event or envelope JSON, anywhere, for any reason. ADR-084 d.2 forbids it: a second hand-maintained source drifts from the first while both suites stay green -- the defect class behind six W3 post-merge fixes. Test inputs are the captured contract payloads and the tool-captured golden scenarios (#1311). ADR-094 d.5 relaxes this ONLY for the existing client replay in `mock-data.ts`, which this slice neither extends nor imitates.

Do NOT write English seller-facing copy. Vietnamese only, second person ("ban"), per S-NFR-4 and S-NFR-12; there is no EN toggle in v1 (`ux-surface.md` F.12 option (a)). An English label, an English empty state, an English error, or an English tooltip is a defect even when it never ships to a Vietnamese seller in the demo walk.

Do NOT let an internal identifier reach seller-facing text. No `workflow_key`, tool name, playbook key, predicate or guard name, stop-reason identifier, `subject_ref`, run id, order id, SKU id or warehouse id in any rendered string (ADR-084 d.5, S-NFR-4). The banned-pattern guard is the floor, not the ceiling: an identifier the regex list happens not to match is still a defect.

Do NOT read the workflow's identity from anything but the seller-facing envelope. Grouping, gating and labelling derive from `recommendation.workflow_name` and the `is_executable` discriminator that `packages/contracts/src/decisions.ts` already carries; `workflow_key` is absent from that envelope by ADR-084 d.3 and must NOT be reintroduced, inferred, reverse-engineered from a title, or smuggled in through a URL segment. If a v1 workflow cannot be distinguished without leaking the taxonomy, STOP AND REPORT (#1793).

Do NOT render a value outside a numeric field's validated range, and do NOT invent the range. Bounds come from the contract descriptor (`packages/contracts/src/review.ts`), never from a component literal; CE-FR-4's stock goal is `0 <= goal < sellable` and RI-NFR-3 forbids a write below the committed quantity. A control that can express an out-of-range value -- an unclamped slider, a free-text number, a spinner without bounds -- is the defect, whether or not a validator catches it afterwards (#1783).

Do NOT change a backend route, response model, payload producer or database row from this slice. Domain is ui-ux, one domain per issue; the producers are named in the issue's Blocked-by list. Do NOT open `apps/dashboard/`, `ios/`, `backend/src/juli_backend/ai/`, `backend/src/juli_backend/workers/` or the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051) -- this epic's doNotLoad list.

Do NOT prove a contract with a `**kwargs` double or a hand-rolled stub of a contract type. Bind every test collaborator to the REAL exported type and the REAL module; a double proves routing, never that the real payload would render. Consumer-without-producer is the failure this wave exists to prevent.
Do NOT build the confirmation sheet (#1779), the deadline list (#1790) or any new fetch path. This slice reads the SAME `/v1/demo/decisions` route on the signed-in path only.
Do NOT compute a count, a deadline or a subject label client-side. Everything rendered traces to a field on the envelope; a derived label is how the demo starts disagreeing with the product.

Do NOT group the fixture array and call it done if #1703/#1320 have not landed. A fixture-fed panel regrouped by a fixture's own `workflowKey` proves nothing about the envelope and reintroduces the taxonomy leak.
